question: Why did opex run over budget in July?

intro.title: Meet Daniel Okafor
intro.text: FP&A Manager, London. Close week, a QBR at 14:00, and every system he owns — SAP, NetSuite, Excel — already awake in one workspace.

hero.title: The day, pre-briefed
hero.text: Before coffee: July variance needs locking before Priya's 14:00 QBR prep — Engineering is $862K over on AWS. The workspace leads with what matters.

kpis.title: Four numbers, live
kpis.text: YTD opex $211.2M against plan. DSO down 3 days to 38. Forecast accuracy 95.1%. Pulled straight from SAP and NetSuite, not last week's deck.

chart.title: The July spike, explained
chart.text: Actual vs budget, month by month. July jumps $1.44M over — the AWS true-up and an early Salesforce renewal. August already tracking back to +1.4%.

ask.title: Drag the number, ask why
ask.text: Daniel drops the opex card into chat and asks the question Priya will ask him. Watch it interrogate three systems at once.

delegate.title: Delegate the chasing
delegate.text: One click: chase the open accruals. It nudges three cost-center owners in Teams — two of three post within 90 minutes, $228K cleared.

autopilot.title: Approvals on autopilot
autopilot.text: Flip the switch. In-policy items like Aisha's $3,214 close-support flights clear themselves; the $86K Adobe renewal still waits for Daniel.

mcp.title: Plugged into everything
mcp.text: Under the hood: live connections to SAP, NetSuite, Workday, Ariba and more. Every answer traces back to a real system call.

recap.title: Friday, in one click
recap.text: The week recap writes itself — bridge delivered, accruals posted, six aged approvals cleared. The Friday report stops being an evening job.

outro.title: More analysis, less chasing
outro.text: Daniel walked into the 14:00 with the bridge done by 11:40. That's the point: the copilot chases, he decides.
